key_insight: A single framework combines a forward predictive model with an inverse generative model to both predict electrolyte properties and propose new formulations — yielding three high-conductivity candidates that were experimentally validated.
problem_solved: Accelerates and automates liquid electrolyte discovery by bridging prediction and inverse design, reducing costly trial-and-error and the fragmented workflow that separates property prediction from candidate generation.
method: Train a forward predictive model to estimate electrolyte properties (e.g., ionic conductivity) from formulation descriptors.
Use an inverse generative model to propose candidate formulations conditioned on target properties.
Integrate predictor + generator in a closed loop to screen and prioritize candidates, followed by experimental validation of top hits.
impact: Demonstrates a practical, experimentally validated blueprint for combining predictive and generative ML in materials discovery — a template ML practitioners can adapt for other formulation-driven problems to speed up R&D.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing forward predictor and inverse generator with a feedback loop to experiments
Predicted vs. measured conductivity scatter plot highlighting the three validated candidates
Schematic of an electrolyte formulation (icons for solvents, salts, additives) to show input space
Bar chart or timeline showing reduced number of experiments/accelerated discovery compared to baseline
paper_title: A unified predictive and generative solution for liquid electrolyte formulation
paper_authors: Zhenze Yang, Yifan Wu, Xu Han, Ziqing Zhang, Haoen Lai
